summary: Stop user-manager stub churn by sharing loaded-only systemd snapshots and remembering terminal execution scopes.

replay.detail: No claim format or replay change.

compatibility.detail: Linux service aliases and worker PIDs resolve from complete loaded-unit snapshots rather than per-name show calls. One process admits a refresh at most every two seconds, enumerates matching loaded units once, and batches properties for at most 128 enumerated names per invocation. Terminal scope names and generation-bound retirement proofs are retained and excluded from later property queries. Scope creation/join freshness prevents cached pre-creation absence from proving retirement. Stale or incomplete snapshots fail closed. Manager commands share single-flight ownership, a three-second invocation deadline followed by kill/reap, and failure backoff from two to sixty seconds. Actual successful controls invalidate observations without bypassing admission.

downtime.detail: Restart the daemon to activate bounded observations and terminal memory. No user-manager reset or state migration is required.

manual.detail: No new configuration. Request-rate, historical-scope, timeout/backoff, unwind and freshness behavior is covered with injected clocks/runners and private manager fixtures; a live manager stall is not exercised.

recovery.detail: A completed admitted refresh replaces stale observations. Kernel reap latency can exceed the command deadline; health is published before cleanup and single-flight remains held until the owned child is reaped.
